blocks.text: B1-19 · Formulas, idioms and proverbs
Lesson overview

A language is made not only of words and rules, but also of phrases already ready: the formulas that are said to those who celebrate, to those who are sick, to those who leave; idiomatic expressions that journalists love ( ⁧حِبْرٌ عَلَى وَرَقٍ⁩ Ink on paper (i.e. dead letter) proverbs that close a speech. In this unit you learn the most important social formulas with their response, about twenty idiomatic expressions frequent in the press, a dozen proverbs with their Italian equivalent and some Egyptian proverb to recognize. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 135–136), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, dictionary (seek full expressions), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. use the most common social formulas and respond in the expected way ( ⁧مَبْرُوك⁩ → ⁧اللهُ يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ⁩ );
2. recognize an idiomatic expression and understand its figurative meaning, without translating it to the letter;
3. understand and translate about twenty idioms in the newspapers;
4. recognize ten classical Arab proverbs and their Italian equivalent;
5. use a proverb at the right time, with formulas that introduce it.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: ⁧إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ does not mean "no" (s). It is the normal formula for the future: ⁧سَأَتَّصِلُ بِكَ غَدًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ I'll call you tomorrow. Sometimes, in the right tone, he hides a kind rejection; but it should not always be felt as a ... perhaps. ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ It is said when you admire something: in many Arab cultures a compliment without this formula may seem to bring bad luck.
4. What is an idiomatic expression

An idiomatic expression ( ⁧تَعْبِيرٌ اصْطِلَاحِيٌّ⁩ ) is a group of words whose meaning is not derived from the individual words: being green does not speak of colors. The sense is figurative ( ⁧مَجَازِيّ⁩ ), not literal ( ⁧حَرْفِيّ⁩ ). How you recognize her. The literal sense does not make sense in the context: an ink in an article on transport, a wall in a news about government. When it happens:
1. search in the dictionary for the whole expression , under the most rare word ( ⁧حِبْرٌ عَلَى وَرَقٍ⁩ below ⁧ح ب ر⁩ );
2. search for an Italian equivalent with the same image or sense;
3. If it's not there, translate the meaning: ⁧ضَرَبَ بِهِ عُرْضَ الحَائِطِ⁩ → • He completely ignored it.

blocks.text: The form of proverbs. Many Arab proverbs are built on a parallelism with rhyme ( ⁧سَجْع⁩ ): ⁧السَّلَامَةُ⁩ / ⁧النَّدَامَةُ⁩ , ⁧قَلَّ⁩ / ⁧دَلَّ⁩ , ⁧جَدَّ⁩ / ⁧وَجَدَ⁩ . That's what makes them easy to remember. ⁧رُبَّ⁩ + indeterminate name to the genitive means                                                  , can happen that sometimes: • • ⁧رُبَّ ضَارَّةٍ نَافِعَةٌ.⁩ A verse that became a proverb. The poet al-Mutanabbī (X century) wrote: ⁧مَا كُلُّ مَا يَتَمَنَّى المَرْءُ يُدْرِكُهُ، تَجْرِي الرِّيَاحُ بِمَا لَا تَشْتَهِي السُّفُنُ⁩ Not all that man desires is achieved: winds blow like ships would not want it. The second half is quoted alone when something goes wrong.
8. Using a proverb

The formulas that introduce it. ⁧وَكَمَا يَقُولُ المَثَلُ⁩ : ... and as the proverb says... ⁧وَكَمَا يُقَالُ⁩ :... • as they say... • ⁧صَدَقَ مَنْ قَالَ⁩ :.......................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................... When. A proverb closes a story, comments a situation, consoles: ⁧رَسَبْتُ فِي الاِمْتِحَانِ، لٰكِنْ رُبَّ ضَارَّةٍ نَافِعَةٌ: الآنَ أَفْهَمُ القَوَاعِدَ أَحْسَنَ⁩ I have failed, but not all evil comes to harm: now I understand grammar better. How much. One is enough: a speech full of proverbs sounds artificial, especially in the mouth of a foreigner. A proverb said at the right time, instead, makes you smile and like it very much.

10. Pronunciation

The rhythm of proverbs. Read the section proverbs 7 aloud with a small pause in the middle and the rhyme clear at the end: fī t-taʾannī s-salāmah (Pause) wa-fī l-ʿaǧalati n-nadāmah. The rhyme words are pronounced "in pause" with the final h just perceptible or mute. The formulas in the speech. The formulas of the section 2 they say fast and without loss: mabrūk, kull sana w-inta ṭayyib (in Egypt), salāmtak, allāh Yisallimak. In the Egyptian language you will feel it that way (EGY-08, EGY-09); in Arabic formal standard are said with desinences.
